source_sync.preserved_differences: Six existing documents retain their independent history and UMC references; only feature hunks applied
source_sync.timing: Feature sources synchronized before final delivery documentation; six independent document histories preserved

visual_review.scope: Six final-commit images inspected with view_image: timing fixture and installed release tab on Ubuntu 24.04, EL8 and EL10; 540 images archived, not all manually reviewed
observations: All 30 timing rows are visible in each reference capture, including the taller EL10 rows; timing names, values, units, bit ranges and full 64-bit raw words are readable
DDR5 tPPD is explicitly Not used; tWRPRE retains its own label; tCL 36, tWRPRE 80 and tREFI 24000 match the synthetic fixture
Controller/channel, rank mask, Gear status and the complete offline-origin and programmed-timing explanation are visible without clipping
The installed release shows the Memory timings tab, target controls and snapshot buttons; initial state has an empty table and disabled copy/save buttons

superseded_attempts.reason: Static review of Intel 743846-001 found rank occupancy resets to 0x0F on empty channels; require nonzero DIMM L/S size before reading timings
Rocky Linux 10 Qt screenshot test required all 30 rows in a fixed 1100 px window; size the reference capture from actual row geometry and verify scrolling in the normal viewport

limits: Live reads require CPUID Intel family 6 model B7 without a hypervisor, PCI 8086:A700 class 060000 and an already enabled MCHBAR
DDR4 supports channel 0 only; DDR5 supports channel 0 or 1; these indices do not identify physical motherboard DIMM slots
Two matching snapshots detect changes but are not atomic hardware measurements; all fixture values are synthetic
Gear division overrides retain encoded values; no timing, frequency, voltage, training or board-controller writes are implemented by this feature
Other AMD, Intel and board-specific protocols, target hardware and Secure Boot validation remain pending
Portable core validation on Windows/macOS is not a full hardware port
